raw_response:
I will keep doing the wheat-maize rotation on my land this year. In Quzhou County, that is the cropping pattern I know best, it matches the local climate, and it is the safest way for me to get stable grain yield without making management too complicated. I am 63, so I will not choose crops that need too much fine hand labor or carry too much market risk. I will plant winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land after wheat harvest. I will use improved seed, not old saved seed, because it is more reliable but still familiar to manage. For wheat, I will use moderate fertilizer, irrigate several times if water allows, and spray a few times mainly for weeds, aphids, and disease. After harvest, I will quickly sow maize, use a bit more nitrogen, irrigate fewer times because the rainy season helps, and spray for weeds and major insects when needed. I will keep tillage simple with rotary tillage because it saves effort and I am used to it.
